history.period: Dvapara Yuga per legend; current structure maintained by a local trust since 1947 with 1990s renovations
history.summary: One of the four ancient Shiva temples said to guard the four corners of Agra, and regarded as the city's oldest sacred site. Legend says Lord Shiva came from Mount Kailash to see the newborn Krishna in Mathura/Gokul; resting here, he vowed that if he could hold baby Krishna he would install a lingam on this spot — and having his wish (mankamna) fulfilled, declared that devotees' wishes would likewise be fulfilled here, hence 'Mankameshwar'. The shivling is entirely covered in silver. On 24 July 2004 a Krishna (Shrinathji) idol was installed under the guidance of Nanaji Bhai of Mathura's Dwarkadhish temple. The sanctum is reached down about 20 steps; devotees must wear traditional Indian attire (dhoti/sari) and no leather items near the deity.

name: Mankameshwar Temple
town_description: Agra, on the banks of the Yamuna in western Uttar Pradesh, was the capital of the Mughal Empire under Akbar, Jahangir and Shah Jahan, and is home to the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri. Alongside its Mughal monuments it is an old Hindu pilgrimage centre, guarded — in local belief — by four ancient Shiva temples set at the four corners of the city.

travel.airport: Pandit Deen Dayal Upadhyay Airport, Agra
travel.railway: Agra Fort railway station (very close); Agra Cantt is the main junction
travel.road: Daresi Road, Rawatpara in Agra's old city near Jama Masjid; avoid four-wheelers, parking is difficult in the narrow lanes

visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:00 AM - 12:00 Noon and 4:00 PM - 9:00 PM, daily (per bhaktibharat)
